002.rootCause: The model was asked about information beyond its training cutoff date and fabricated a plausible but wrong answer.
002.missingCapability: Fact Retrieval — the model cannot know what it was never trained on. Real-time data access or fact-check verification is needed.
002.recommendedFix: For factual questions, add a retrieval tool or set knowledge cutoff expectations. Models hallucinate confidently when pushed past their knowledge boundary.

generic.rootCause: The agent encountered an unexpected failure during execution.
generic.missingCapability: Review the runtime trace to identify which step failed and what engineering capability could have prevented it.
generic.recommendedFix: Examine the event timeline to find the failure point, then add the corresponding harness dimension or loop configuration.

level_1_raw.description: A model alone is not an agent. With no harness, the runner cannot ground tools, persist work, or stop on real evidence — expect hallucinated tools, corrosion, and abandoned tasks.
level_1_raw.tutorial: Proposition: Agent = Model + Harness. A model alone is not an agent — without harness infrastructure it cannot ground tools, persist work, or stop on real evidence. Without tracing you would only see a failure, not why it failed. In this simulator tracing is always on so you can always see the full trace.

level_2_harness.description: Same model, different harness — results diverge sharply. Unlock all seven harness dimensions. Still no loop, so a single failed test abandons the task.
level_2_harness.tutorial: Proposition: Same model, different harness → huge difference. Tool Registry, Retry Policy, Timeout Guard, Sandbox Isolation, Context Manager, State Persistence, and Permission Layer change outcomes far more than swapping the model.

level_3_loop.description: Loop on evidence, not confidence. Configure trigger, goal, state/action policy, evidence, feedback, and stop rules. Loop engineering ≠ prompt engineering.
level_3_loop.tutorial: Proposition: Evidence, not confidence. Loop ≠ prompt engineering — stop on real checks (tests, schema, review), not "agent says done."

level_4_loop_stack.description: Two loops can cooperate or fight. Pick a template: a single verification loop, or a verification loop nested inside an improvement loop.
level_4_loop_stack.tutorial: Proposition: Loops can cooperate or fight. The dual template nests fast inner verification inside slower outer improvement; the factory template sequences Plan → Build → Test → Review → Release.

level_5_graph.description: The graph decides who runs next — not what the agent does. Conditional edges route control flow; failure states must always have a recovery path.
level_5_graph.tutorial: Proposition: Graph = who runs next — not a knowledge graph. Conditional edges route control flow; every failure state needs a recovery path. A simple single-agent task often needs no graph.

level_6_agent_system.description: Plan → Build → Test → Review → Release. Combine the full harness, a factory loop template, and export the blueprint as real code.
level_6_agent_system.tutorial: Proposition: Agent System = the full stack. Combine the full harness, the factory loop template, and export the blueprint as real LangGraph code.

harness.title: Harness Configuration
harness.toolRegistryDesc: Expose a real, typed tool API so the model cannot invent tools
harness.retryPolicyDesc: Provide structured retry scaffolding — a loop needs this mechanism to actually retry
harness.timeoutGuardDesc: Cap the run boundary (tokens or iterations) before it explodes
harness.sandboxIsolationDesc: Execute code in an isolated environment that cannot corrupt the host
harness.contextManagerDesc: Ground the model with fresh files, specs, and prior run state
harness.statePersistenceDesc: Version workspace changes so edits do not overwrite each other
harness.permissionLayerDesc: Define an allowlist — capability is not permission

loop.title: Loop Anatomy
loop.enabledDesc: Allow the agent to iterate until evidence or budget says stop

loopStack.title: Loop Stack
loopStack.singleHint: Single Loop is the Level 3 loop — the Loop panel governs its behavior. Pick Dual or Factory to run a preset loop-stack template.
loopStack.lockedNote: Preset — click a field to see why it exists

why.trigger: A loop needs a trigger to know when to start observing.
why.goal: The goal is a concrete state, not a vague instruction.
why.evidence: Without evidence, "done" means nothing — FALSE_COMPLETION becomes likely.
why.feedback: Feedback must describe why it failed so the next attempt is different.
why.stopOn: Stop on evidence pass, never on agent self-report.
why.maxIterations: An iteration cap turns an infinite loop into a bounded one.
why.inner: The inner loop verifies each attempt quickly.
why.outer: The outer loop improves the overall approach after inner verification.
why.innerEvidence: Fast, cheap checks for each edit.
why.outerEvidence: Slower, stronger sign-off gates the final release.
why.plan: Decompose the goal into concrete steps.
why.review: A second pair of eyes; rejection sends it back to build.

reflections.reflect_test_fail: Last run failed an assertion. This time, read the full error before editing.
reflections.reflect_wrong_file: Last run edited the wrong file. This time, follow the stack trace to the real path.
reflections.reflect_off_by_one: Last run had an off-by-one boundary bug. This time, check loop and index bounds.
reflections.reflect_dependency: Last run missed a dependency import. This time, confirm the module is in scope.

failureHints.HALLUCINATION: The model called a tool that does not exist — with no Tool Registry it invents APIs.
failureHints.TOOL_FAILURE: A real tool returned garbage. Tools can be called but still be unreliable — only a verification loop catches this.
failureHints.FILE_CORROSION: The agent overwrote its own work. Without State Persistence, each edit destroyed the previous one.
failureHints.MEMORY_STACK_OVERFLOW: The agent ran out of memory buffer. Too many steps without enough capacity and it forgot the task.
failureHints.CONTEXT_OVERFLOW: The context window filled during retries. History accumulated until the agent could no longer process new information.
failureHints.STALE_CONTEXT: The agent acted on an outdated snapshot. Without a Context Manager it keeps working from a stale view of the world.
failureHints.FALSE_COMPLETION: The agent stopped because it said "done" — not because evidence passed. Claims are not facts.
failureHints.PERMISSION_ERROR: The agent attempted an action outside its boundary. Capability ≠ Permission — define a Permission Layer.
failureHints.DEADLOCK: The control graph has a failure state with no recovery path. Every on_fail edge must reach a recovery node.
failureHints.INFINITE_LOOP_TRAP: The agent looped without progress: fail → same action → fail. Stop rules or iteration caps were missing or too weak.
failureHints.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: The run hit the run boundary cap (tokens or iterations). Timeout Guard stopped the agent before it could finish.
failureHints.TASK_ABANDONED: The agent quit after the first failure. With no loop enabled, a single test fail ended the run.
failureHints.UNSAFE_EXECUTION: A destructive action ran without Sandbox Isolation and corrupted the environment.

failureFixes.HALLUCINATION: Enable Tool Registry in Harness so the model can only call real tools.
failureFixes.TOOL_FAILURE: Keep the Tool Registry, but add a verification loop that checks tool output before trusting it.
failureFixes.FILE_CORROSION: Enable State Persistence in Harness so edits are versioned.
failureFixes.MEMORY_STACK_OVERFLOW: Raise Memory Capacity, or enable Context Manager to manage state.
failureFixes.CONTEXT_OVERFLOW: Raise Memory Capacity, tighten state_policy, or split work with a Graph.
failureFixes.STALE_CONTEXT: Enable Context Manager so the agent re-reads current files and run state.
failureFixes.FALSE_COMPLETION: Set stop_on to evidence_pass and set evidence to a real check — never agent self-report.
failureFixes.PERMISSION_ERROR: Enable Permission Layer and define an allowlist for the agent's actions.
failureFixes.DEADLOCK: Add a recovery node and route every on_fail edge to it.
failureFixes.INFINITE_LOOP_TRAP: Set stop_on to evidence_pass (or budget_or_max) and raise max_iterations if needed.
failureFixes.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: Raise the run boundary cap, or reduce max_iterations / tighten the loop.
failureFixes.TASK_ABANDONED: Enable the Loop and set evidence + stop_on so the agent can recover.
failureFixes.UNSAFE_EXECUTION: Enable Sandbox Isolation so destructive actions cannot corrupt the host.

tool.question: Can it act safely and with permission?

memory.question: Can it hold state without overflowing?

observation.question: Does it see accurately, without stale context?

loop_discipline.question: Can it iterate and stop on evidence?

execution.question: Can it finish within budget and structure?
